newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds descend in directional trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds descend in directional trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities neared the end of their trading session lower for the third straight day, with discount coupons bearing the brunt of the losses.
In late trading, pass-throughs were off 2/32 to 10/32 in most coupons while comparable Treasuries were off 5/32 to 10/32.
Trading activity was mostly directional and yield spreads continued to narrow modestly to U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.
Cynthia Rivera, mortgage strategist at BZW Securities Inc, said the recent narrowing of yield spreads is a result of "a combination of a lot of little things."

Over the past few days, the mortgage-backed market witnessed a reduction in implied volatility, an increase in buying for commercial mortgage obligations (CMOs) and real estate mortgage investment conduits (REMICs) and an easing in originations, Rivera said.
"But where there is a risk is if the (Treasury) market does rally from here just a little -- it will just widen off its lows," she said.
Earlier on Friday, NationsBanc unleashed a bid list comprising about $1 billion of adjustable-rate mortgages that was snapped-up by eager and willing dealers, traders said.
One regional trader called the deal "well-executed."

By late afternoon Friday, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 9/32 at 99-13/32, yielding 107 basis points aver the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 9/32 lower as well, at 99-10/32 and 99-15/32, respectively.
